messages:
ana: Heads up — customer on Safari (iOS 16.4) seeing partial SSE payloads from /v1/streaming/chat then connection drops and EventSource reconnect loop. Happens behind Fastly CDN.

devon: Got a session id? any error body or client-side logs?

maria-cs: Customer session: sess_03b9c. They reported ~30s of tokens then a midstream close. Billing showed repeated small token charges (appear like reconnects).

kai: Repro steps from the browser console would help. Can you try incognito + disable service worker and confirm? Also need a request/response capture from the edge.

ana: (oops meant ana) Attached the client console: 
``` 
EventSource onerror -> readyState 2, then new EventSource created
Logs: "The connection was interrupted"
```

kai: On the server side we see 200 then a 304 for the same SSE URL during the session. 304s are coming midstream from Fastly when origin sends Last-Modified. That will confuse browsers.

james-eng-runtime: 304 midstream is definitely wrong for streaming endpoints. We should never return conditional responses for chunked/text/event-stream. Looks like edge caching rules applied because endpoint matched a generic /v1/* rule.

rachel-eng-sre: Quick check — Fastly had a rule to cache anything with path /v1/* unless Authorization present, but it was using Vary: Authorization incorrectly and sending 304s when If-Modified-Since/If-None-Match hit. On 304 the edge strips Authorization and some headers on the passthrough which makes the origin treat it differently. Safari then sees truncated stream.

devon: Customer repro (simplified):
1) Open Safari
2) new EventSource('/v1/streaming/chat?session=sess_03b9c', { withCredentials: true })
3) After ~20-30s you get a partial event then error and immediate reconnects

kai: Curl repro (server-side sequence):
```
# initial connect
curl -i -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.example/v1/streaming/chat?session=sess_03b9c
# we see 200, streaming chunks
# later edge responds to a conditional request with 304 and short Content-Length, connection closed
```

ana (ana): Tried with Service Worker disabled — issue still occurs. Incognito same. But in chrome it doesn't reproduce (only Safari).

james-eng-runtime: Safari is more sensitive to 304 + chunked responses for EventSource. Also some polyfills mask it; the polyfill will sometimes keep the old socket open. But this customer is using native EventSource.

rachel-eng-sre: Temporary mitigation options:
- Configure edge to never cache SSE endpoints (Cache-Control: no-store or Cache-Control: private, no-transform, max-age=0)
- Ensure origin responses for event-stream never send Last-Modified/Etag so conditional requests aren't attempted
- Have edge pass through Authorization and avoid transforming responses for these paths

devon: Can we patch the origin to add a specific header on SSE responses: `Cache-Control: no-store, no-transform` and `Vary:` (empty) and remove ETag?

james-eng-runtime: Yes we can return: 
```
Cache-Control: no-store, no-transform, must-revalidate
Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://customer.app
Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization, Content-Type
```
That will stop conditional caching.

maria-cs: Customer asked for ETA and workaround. They can't switch browsers. Also asked for a billing credit due to reconnect churn.

rachel-eng-sre: Immediate actions:
- Eng-sre to deploy Fastly rule to bypass cache for /v1/streaming/* (edge change) — ETA: 90m
- Eng-runtime to push header update to streaming handler to set no-store & remove ETag — ETA: 2h
- Support to offer credit for excessive reconnects this morning — maria-cs will handle communication

kai: Small note: for customers using polyfills or older Safari, a fallback server heartbeat (comment comment: `: heartbeat\n\n` every 15s) helps detect liveness and keeps connection less likely to be closed by intermediaries.

devon: Also verify Access-Control-Expose-Headers if clients rely on custom headers. And ensure OPTIONS preflight returns 204 with proper CORS headers and not a cached 304. Safari sometimes turns an OPTIONS 304 into a broken preflight.

james-eng-runtime: Good call. We'll add an explicit preflight for streaming routes in the origin: return 204 + Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET, OPTIONS and include Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization. No caching on OPTIONS.

ana: TL;DR for support reply to customer: "We're seeing Fastly conditional caching (304) applied to your streaming requests which can truncate SSE in Safari. We're pushing an edge bypass and header changes; temporary workaround is to disable caching on SSE endpoints or we can flip the edge rule server-side. We'll issue credits for reconnect churn." :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: deploy:edge-rule-bypass /v1/streaming/* scheduled by rachel-eng-sre — started

rachel-eng-sre: Will update thread when change is live and include a curl to verify 200 streaming without ETag.

maria-cs: I'll message the customer with the workaround and offer credits. Thanks all :heart:
